RESULT — BCG vaccination odds ratio on COVID-19 severity (ordinal proportional-odds model).

Primary full-sample model (n=1000, severity 0..4, placebo reference):
BCG OR = 1.0910, 95% CI 0.7699–1.5462, p = 0.624. Odds of being in a higher COVID-19 severity category are ~9% higher for BCG-vaccinated vs placebo HCWs, but this is NOT significant (p=0.62; CI spans 1). BCG vaccination shows no statistically significant effect on COVID-19 severity after adjusting for prior medical history count, patients interaction frequency, and their interaction.

Coefficients (predictors):
- bcg (BCG vs placebo): coef 0.0871, SE 0.178, exp 1.091, p=0.624
- mhcount_c (prior medical-history count, centered; +1 condition): coef 0.1743, exp 1.190, p=0.273
- pseen_c (patients_seen midpoint, centered; +1 patient/week): coef 0.0094, exp 1.009, p=0.0005
- mhXp (mhcount_c × pseen_c interaction): coef 0.0086, exp 1.009, p=0.048
Thresholds 0/1=1.794, 1/2=-0.661, 2/3=0.588, 3/4=-0.045 (model converged, BFGS, LL=-572.8, AIC=1162).

Sensitivity (restricted to 151 COVID patients with numeric severity, levels 1..4): BCG OR = 1.1615, 95% CI 0.6243–2.1610, p=0.637 — same conclusion (non-significant, positive direction).

Variable construction & outcome breakdown: outcome 0 = no COVID AE (n=849: BCG 423 / Placebo 426), 1..4 = max AESEV over patient's COVID AE rows (1: n=54 [29/25], 2: n=79 [35/44], 3: n=11 [8/3], 4: n=7 [5/2]); 43 COVID patients with all-missing AESEV kept at level 0. Confirmed ordered with observed levels 0<1<2<3<4.
